syntax: SELECT DISTINCT column_name FROM table_name ORDER BY column_name;
documentation: DISTINCT removes duplicate rows after the result expressions are evaluated. When several columns are selected, uniqueness applies to the complete combination.
inputs: One or more selected result expressions.
caution: DISTINCT is not a replacement for defining the intended data relationship. Add ORDER BY for a predictable display order.
scenarios: List customers who appear in an order export.
Build a list of available service categories.
Find the unique statuses used by imported data.
title: Find unique customer names
problem: Return the distinct customer values from orders, sorted by customer ascending. Keep one NULL value if any customer is NULL; SQLite sorts it before text in ascending order.
goal: Use DISTINCT or an equivalent approach that demonstrates the same concept.
hint: Select DISTINCT customer and order by customer.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT query against the example tables.
SELECT 1;

tests.name: Repeated names
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER, status TEXT); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 'Micki', 100, 'paid'), (2, 'Ava', 200, 'paid'), (3, 'Micki', 300, 'paid');

tests.name: Repeated NULLs
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER, status TEXT); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, NULL, 100, 'paid'), (2, NULL, 200, 'paid'), (3, 'Ava', 300, 'paid');
